The previous pin fixed the compile-time walk's key and said in its own entry
that the runtime one still keyed on the effect, untested. It was worse there.

The fixture needs three things at once: the perform behind a frame fence so
the lexical walk cannot answer, a second declarer so the op is ambiguous and
the singleton walk declines, and a split-effect pair with the NON-declaring
handler innermost. tests/frontier/mn-split-effect-evidence.mn returned 15
where 33 is correct — zero diagnostics, clean assemble, no trap. Where the
compile-time version emitted a call to a named arm that does not exist and the
assembler objected, this one indexed a live arm region and ran. Banked RED
before anything was fixed.

THE ROOT WAS THE LAYOUT, NOT THE WALK. op_slot is documented as a position
into an effect's immutable op-list and every reader indexes the arm region by
it, but set_at_extend only grew a group to the highest slot THAT handler
implements. A handler covering one op of a two-op effect laid a ONE-slot
region, so the other op's slot was ABSENT rather than zero and the read went
past the region. The layout promised density over the EFFECT's ops and
delivered density over the HANDLER's. pad_group_to_effect_ops closes it there
instead of at each reader, and that is what makes the declaring test readable:
node_arm_at asks the record the same question handler_declares_op asks the
groups.

mentl/3b19771:
ev_perform_entry's broken-promise floor loaded 0 - 8: out of bounds by
construction on small memories, silently IN bounds once the module
carried the full 65536 pages (2fc7544) — 0xFFFFFFF8 + 4 fits exactly.
Every evidence miss then returned the virgin word instead of trapping,
and an unfilled-pair cascade surfaced as an indirect call type mismatch
frames away from the miss: the consumer read the postmortem's own
breadcrumbs at addresses 0 and 4 back as record and base. Load 0 - 1
instead — a four-byte read crossing 2^32 is out of bounds at every
wasm32 memory size, the full pages included.

mentl/3b60230:
Two drift fixes from the post-cascade audit, both surfaced by
following CLAUDE.md's just-extended discipline:

heap_base() — single-source-of-truth substrate constant in
  backends/wasm.ka. The literal `4096` lived in two places
  (emit_match_arms_mixed's threshold + comments throughout); now
  one helper, every consumer reads through it. Future change to
  the threshold lands in one place. Crystallized in CLAUDE.md as
  a bug-class warning.

MatchShape ADT — drift mode 8 (string-keyed-when-structured /
  int-coded-when-ADT) target. The classifier returned 0/1/2 ints
  driving emit_match_arms's dispatch; H6 discipline says every
  enum-as-int is an ADT begging to exist. Refactored:

    type MatchShape
      = ShapePureNullary
      | ShapePureFielded
      | ShapeMixed

    classify_arms_mode    → classify_arms_shape (returns MatchShape)
    emit_match_arms_uniform takes MatchShape
    filter_arms_by_mode   → filter_arms_by_shape
    shape_eq helper for variant equality
    All `mode == N` becomes `match shape { ShapeXxx => ... }`

The dispatch is now H6-exhaustive: a future MatchShape variant
forces every consumer site to handle it explicitly. The integer
fallthrough where I'd written `if mode == 2 ... else ...` is gone.

Both fixes named in CLAUDE.md as load-bearing protocols:
  - heap_base + bug class warning about HEAP_BASE collision risk
  - MatchShape pattern as exemplar of drift 8 ("flag/mode-as-int")

perennials/3b03962:
The invisible mass that casts a photo standee's shadow wrote depth as well
as colour-nothing, so it could occlude the very photo it stands in front of:
a plant she photographed would show the paper behind it wherever the hidden
crown crossed the billboard. depthWrite is off now; the shadow still casts,
because casting runs through the shadow pass and does not care about the
main pass's depth.

And importing a yard file swallowed the storage-refusal flag. A client
opening a plan on a full phone was told "Opened" while nothing reached the
disk, which is the silent loss every other write in this app is careful to
say out loud. importYardFile returns whether the disk took it, and the Yards
page says so when it did not.
noodles/3b42b90:
The header tap lands on the Sound page (the play surface Morgan meant),
not the mixer strip; long-press keeps Track Options. The Sound sheet now
takes the full height under the transport and fits every control on a
phone with zero scrolling: the morph pad is the flexible element and
absorbs what the fixed rows leave, colors sit in one six-across row, and
the drum one-shots fold to a 2x2 grid. Receipt at the A16's 360x780
viewport: all four tracks plus both drum banks fit (scrollHeight <=
clientHeight) with the pad no smaller than 260 px in the tallest case;
smoke asserts the tap-and-fit permanently.

?perf in the URL overlays pull-only diagnostics for the couch: rAF fps,
jank count, worst frame gap, audio-clock rate vs wall clock (sustained
below 1.00x = the audio thread starving, the stutter quantified), and the
baseLatency+outputLatency estimate the pie clock leans on — if Android
reports a bogus outputLatency there, the pies lead the ear and that is
the next fix (a manual latency offset).
noodles/3b0a66f:
The drum rack now plays samples by default. Sixteen one-shots across
four kits (street, warm, dusty, 808), and they're ours outright:
scripts/make-samples.mjs synthesizes them offline with the layering
realtime synthesis on a phone can't afford — click transients over
pitch-enveloped subs, modal snare bodies under shaped noise, six
detuned metallic partials per hat, multi-burst claps — then bakes the
saturation in. 412 KB total, deterministic seeds, bundled under
public/samples/ (same-origin, CSP-clean, nothing fetched from anyone).

Sample kits are corners on the same morph pad: hits crossfade the two
dominant kits' one-shots with the same top-2 equal-power rule as the
melodic layers, and the color slot applies unchanged. A per-voice
picker pins any bundled one-shot or a WAV you load from your device
(session-scoped; persistence is an open fork). The synth kit stays as
a second bank, the dice rolls both (samples weighted), and a buffer
that fails to load falls back to the synth voice instead of silence.
Buffer playback also costs less DSP than MembraneSynth synthesis, so
the default cold open got cheaper on weak phones.

Per-hit nodes bind to the graph's own context: Tone.Offline restores
the live context before rendering runs, so ambient-context nodes
created inside render callbacks die cross-context. Trims are measured
in the speaker band (>80 Hz), where the sample bank sits within 1.3 dB
and all eight kits within 2.3; the 808's flat RMS runs hot by design
because its energy is sub-tail, with the lowest peaks of any kit.
